payload.name: Validate State Memory Timing in Count Questions
payload.description: Use when a question asks how many items a person had/owned as of a specific past time and a retrieved state memory appears to contradict a non-zero answer.
content: When a count question specifies 'as of <date>', do not treat a state memory as conclusive evidence unless its world_start/world_end interval includes that date; a state with no world_end and start before the target may be outdated.

If such a state is retrieved, run additional searches for acquisition events (adopted, bought, got, received, acquired) dated before the target date, including searches for named instances if any names appear in other retrieved memories.
Only finalize a count after confirming no acquisition events before the target date exist; otherwise sum the distinct acquisitions before the target date.

solves: When a count question includes 'as of <date>', a state memory with no end date and start before that date may be stale, causing undercounts when later acquisition events are missed. This rule applies to any 'how many X as of <date>' retrieval and requires temporal validation of state memories plus supplementary acquisition-event searches.
